It was 2007 when my mom started having pain in one of her eys. By that time she had been using contact lenses for more than 30 years, from you know the glass contact lenses back in the 70s when she was a teenager to soft lenses. Well she started with pain in one of her eyes, she went to the ophthalmologist and they said it was a keratitis, they gave her some eye drops and send her home. One week after my mom started having photophobia, we were going to the hospital everyday and every time they said "it's just a keratitis caused by a fungus infection, you will be good in a few days, just keep using the eyedrops". She got to a point that she couldn't sleep because the pain was excruciating. It took them 3 more weeks to finally realized "this is not okay" and do a biopsy. She had an infection but it was not a fungus, it was acanthamoeba and by point her other eye was infected as well. They put her on a regimen, 3 different eye drops, phmb and others, it was expensive and she still had photophobia. The day came when they had to put her on the transplant list for one of her corneas, the other eye healed. 2 days after she had surgery. She recovered her sight (not fully but almost) but after surgery entered into a deep depression. A few months of not working and having to be confined to her bedroom without being able to see light wrecked her mental health. 
She is good now. Thanks to the third doctor, that third opinion saved her sight.
